verses: تَعْرُجُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِى يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُۥ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ
يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ يَوَدُّ ٱلْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِى مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍۭ بِبَنِيهِ
وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِم مُّشْفِقُونَ
إِلَّا عَلَىٰٓ أَزْوَٰجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ
فَمَنِ ٱبْتَغَىٰ وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْعَادُونَ
أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ
فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْمَشَٰرِقِ وَٱلْمَغَٰرِبِ إِنَّا لَقَٰدِرُونَ
عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ خَيْرًا مِّنْهُمْ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ
فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا۟ وَيَلْعَبُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُوا۟ يَوْمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى يُوعَدُونَ
يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ سِرَاعًا كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ
خَٰشِعَةً أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمُ ٱلَّذِى كَانُوا۟ يُوعَدُونَ

leads.title: Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance ↔ The ascending stairways: the day of fifty thousand years and the steadfast worshippers
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Catalogue of the righteous man: no eating on the mountains, no idols, no adultery, no menstrual intercourse, no oppression, returns pledges, feeds the hungry, clothes the naked, no interest (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance: Exhortation: cast away your transgressions and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit; why will you die?; Test case of three generations: righteous father, violent son, and a grandson who sees his father's sins and does not imitate them; Whether one person can carry another's sin [divergence between the texts]; No one may excuse himself on judgment day because his ancestors associated partners; If the wicked turns from his sins, none of his transgressions will be remembered; if the righteous turns away, his righteousness is forgotten; Proverb 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes and the children's teeth are set on edge', abolished by God; Whether repentance has a time limit [divergence between the texts]; People complain 'the way of the Lord is not fair'; God answers that it is their ways that are unfair; God does not desire the death of the wicked but that he turn from his way and live; A cloak taken in pledge must be returned before sunset; 'The soul that sins, it shall die': the son does not bear the father's iniquity nor the father the son's; Whoever does good does it for his own soul; whoever does evil, it is against it; and 4 more.

Only in The ascending stairways: the day of fifty thousand years and the steadfast worshippers: A day whose measure is fifty thousand years, during which angels and the Spirit ascend to God; The dead come out of the graves hurrying as if racing to a standing stone (nusub); Humankind was created restless (halu'): fretful when evil touches him, grudging when good comes; On the day the sky will be like molten metal or dregs of oil (muhl); The angels and the Spirit (al-ruh) ascend to God by stairways (ma'arij); God is 'Lord of the ascending ways'; The faithful guard their private parts except with their wives or those their right hands possess; beyond that is transgression; In the wealth of the righteous is a known right (haqq ma'lum) for the beggar and the deprived; God is able to replace a people with others better than they, and none can outrun him; On the day no friend asks after friend; a man flees his brother, mother, father, wife and sons, each wholly occupied with himself; On the day the mountains will be like (carded, dyed) wool ('ihn); No man can ransom his brother or give God a ransom (kofer) for him; the redemption of life is too costly [divergence between the texts]; A thousand years in God's sight are like yesterday when it passes, or a watch in the night [divergence between the texts]; and 5 more.

matches.note: Catalogue defining the righteous: Ezekiel lists ʾel he-hārîm lōʾ ʾākāl ... ʾet ʾēšet rēʿēhû lōʾ ṭimmēʾ ... ḥăvōlātô ḥôv yāšîv ... laḥmô le-rāʿēv yittēn; Q 70:22-34 lists alladhīna hum ʿalā ṣalātihim dāʾimūn, fī amwālihim ḥaqqun maʿlūmun li-s-sāʾili wa-l-maḥrūm, li-furūjihim ḥāfiẓūn, li-amānātihim wa-ʿahdihim rāʿūn. Shared: sexual restraint, faithfulness with pledges and trusts, food for the poor. Ezekiel's items are cultic and judicial (mountains, menstruation, interest); the Quran's begin and end with prayer.
